discovery: Dynamical symmetries and supersymmetry in nuclear and molecular spectra: the Interacting Boson Model and algebraic (spectrum-generating) methods in quantum many-body physics
motivation: Francesco Iachello showed that the complicated collective spectra of atomic nuclei are organized by dynamical symmetries. With the late Akito Arima he created the Interacting Boson Model. Its U(6) algebra, with the U(5), SU(3) and O(6) limits, predicted whole families of states, electromagnetic transition rates and selection rules. Precise spectroscopy worldwide later confirmed these predictions, including the O(6) spectra of platinum isotopes. Iachello then proposed supersymmetry in physics: nuclear supersymmetry unites bosonic and fermionic nuclei in a single supermultiplet, and experiments on the Au-Pt quartet confirmed it, one of the few places where supersymmetry has been verified experimentally. He extended the same algebraic ideas to molecules through the vibron model, and to quantum phase transitions with the E(5) and X(5) critical-point symmetries. His work unified nuclear, molecular and hadronic spectroscopy under one algebraic framework that makes predictions, and it has shaped a generation of physicists.
